maria: quick heads-up — after landing the optimized matmul kernel (tiling change) we see a PP run regression on 32xA100: end-to-end token latency +18% at seq=2048, microbatch=4.

akshay: hmm, is this visible in the timeline view or only aggregate? any flamegraphs?

maria: timeline. attaching short prof snapshot (copied):

```
step  | compute_ms | comm_ms | idle_ms
1    | 12.4       | 1.8     | 0.6
2    | 11.9       | 5.2     | 5.3  <-- big comm stall during KV refill/1F1B
3    | 12.0       | 1.7     | 0.8
```

lee: looks like 1F1B bubble widened at the second stage. Could be all-reduce algo or buffer sizes. what's NCCL settings?

nina: @maria can you repro with NCCL_ALGO=ring and then hierarchical? also try increasing microbatch to 8 and see bubble shrink.

maria: tried ring vs tree: tree reduces all-reduce time by ~30% but increases some small-host-sync overhead. microbatch=8 reduces bubble but hurts tail latency for small requests.

akshay: curious if the new matmul tiling changed when compute finishes relative to comm schedule. if compute finishes later it reduces overlap, so effective comm increases.

maria: that matches: the kernel sped up first gemm but shifted layer timing so the all-reduce launch got delayed. probed kernel timings:

```
layer  | gemm_finish_ms | allreduce_start_ms
enc1   | 10.1           | 10.3
enc2   | 9.2            | 14.5  <-- gap
```

lee: two quick experiments:
- pad microbatch to align with pipeline stages (pad to 16 tokens)
- enable async all-reduce (torch.distributed.all_reduce(..., async_op=True)) + explicit wait at merge

nina: also try enabling NCCL_ASYNC_ERROR=1? jk. but set NCCL_IB_DISABLE=0 and NCCL_COLLNET=0 depending on topology.

infra-bot: perf-run 1730001240 started on ci-pp32. configs: microbatch=4 -> 8, NCCL_ALGO=tree

maria: CI run shows bubble drop from 18%->6% with microbatch 8 + tree all-reduce, but cost per token up ~4% for small seq. We need better middle ground.

akshay: idea: adaptive microbatching per-request-size. small requests use microbatch=4 with priority fast path, long seqs use 8. Or dynamic 1F1B scheduler that shifts when all-reduce lag exceeds threshold.

lee: could also try sharding KV cache slightly differently so refill overlaps with compute on earlier ranks.

nina: action items:
- maria: add timeline screenshots + exact kernel build id to the issue
- akshay: prototype async-allreduce wrapper and gate by topology
- lee: run KV-refill overlap sim with microbatch sweep

maria: file created: perf/pp/1730001234-pp-bubble-squeeze-notes.md (circling back with traces)

akshay: thanks — will sync tomorrow in 1:1. :thumbsup:

maria: :rocket:
